images.title: A pencil in cm and a wall in m
images.purpose: Show why the pencil gets cm and the classroom wall gets m: a pencil of 17 cm beside a ruler, and a wall of 8 m beside a tape, each with the fitting unit chip and the other chip crossed out.
images.composition: Two panels, a pencil with a short ruler on the left and a long classroom wall with a tape on the right, each with a green chip and a crossed grey chip below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two panels split by one thin grey #6B7280 vertical line at x 728 (y 80 to 736). LEFT PANEL: exactly 1 pencil, a flat horizontal rectangle 340 px long and 36 px high (x 194 to 534, y 300 to 336) filled amber #E69F00 with a reddish purple #CC79A7 eraser square 36 by 36 px at its left end (x 194 to 230) and a triangular tip at its right end; under it one ruler strip, a yellow rectangle 340 px by 50 px (x 194 to 534, y 360 to 410) with exactly 18 tick marks, one every 20 px, so 17 equal parts, and the long tick marks at x 194 and x 534 only. Below, a green #009E73 rounded rectangle chip 180 by 64 px (x 194 to 374, y 480 to 544) with the text 17 cm, and next to it a grey #6B7280 chip 180 by 64 px (x 394 to 574, y 480 to 544) with the text 17 m crossed out by 2 vermilion #D55E00 diagonal lines. RIGHT PANEL: exactly 1 classroom wall, a rectangle 560 px wide and 150 px high (x 808 to 1368, y 250 to 400) filled pale teal #0072B2 at 25 percent with exactly 7 thin vertical lines dividing it into 8 equal sections of 70 px; under it one tape line from x 808 to x 1368 at y 440 with exactly 9 tick marks, one every 70 px. Below, a green chip 180 by 64 px (x 808 to 988, y 480 to 544) with the text 8 m, and next to it a grey chip (x 1008 to 1188, y 480 to 544) with the text 8 cm crossed out by 2 vermilion diagonal lines. Above each panel, centred at y 140, the caption in 44 px: Pencil on the left, Wall on the right. In all: 1 pencil, 1 wall, 2 rulers or tapes, 4 chips. All shapes are flat fills with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px), no shadows and no gradients; all text is dark #1F2937 sans-serif. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a pencil or wall with a different number of ruler parts, tape ticks or sections
any chip text other than the four listed
images.takeaway: Short things take cm and long things take m, so the number sounds sensible.
images.description: A pencil of 17 cm beside a ruler and a classroom wall of 8 m beside a tape, with the fitting unit chip and the other chip crossed out.
images.context: Concept image for Choosing a Unit That Fits. It follows the idea of the Let Us Find table in your maths book (short things in cm, long things in m) and shows the concept's own example, a pencil and a classroom wall (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Let the student say why the crossed chips do not fit. The slip to watch: writing 17 m for a pencil because 17 is the right number.
